task: Close #94 (apparent-size brownfield snapshot), #93 (permanent fail-open on a startup report failure), and #92 (unbounded per-cycle usage-report cost) -- the three items PR #91 documented as accepted limitations rather than scope for #90's fix

events.summary: Scoped to the brownfield shrink guard's snapshot accuracy (#94), its prime lifecycle (#93), and its per-cycle usage-report cost (#92) -- the same file regions PR #91's doc comments named as the accepted-limitation follow-ups. No API, CRD, chart, or RBAC surface touched; /health semantics untouched; metrics/UI/history/cleanup/orphan sizing deliberately left reading apparent size unchanged, since GetDirAllocatedSize has exactly one caller (the brownfield snapshot) by design

#94: GetDirUsages' apparent-size filepath.Walk (info.Size()) biases in both directions against real quota accounting -- a sparse file's apparent size overstates its true disk cost (over-suspicion), and many small files understate it via per-file block rounding (missed suspicion). Reproduced by asserting the relation directly: a 1GiB sparse file's apparent size equals its allocated size when summed via info.Size(), which is the wrong relation for a KB-block-charging backend

Added status.GetDirAllocatedSize (internal/status/dirsize_unix.go, //go:build unix): filepath.Walk summing st.Blocks*512, deduplicated by (Dev,Ino) so hardlinks aren't double-counted, with a comma-ok *syscall.Stat_t assertion falling back to info.Size() per-file; dirsize_other.go supplies the same signature (apparent-size fallback) under //go:build !unix so the package still compiles elsewhere. Wired into status.GetDirUsagesStrict only -- GetDirSize/GetDirUsages and every existing consumer (metrics, web UI, history, cleanup, orphan sizing) are untouched

Deliberate breakage: reverted dirsize_unix.go's sum from st.Blocks*512 to info.Size() and re-ran TestGetDirAllocatedSize_SparseFileBelowApparentSize, which failed with 'GetDirAllocatedSize = 1073741824, want < apparent size 1073741824' -- confirming the sparse-file relation actually depends on the blocks-not-apparent-size accounting, then reverted the breakage and re-confirmed green
events.scope: internal/status GetDirAllocatedSize/GetDirUsagesStrict, exercised against real tmpfs/APFS files (sparse truncation, many small files, a hardlink pair) with no CommandRunner involved for the walk itself

events.summary: #93: primeAppliedQuotasFromDiskOnce was sync.Once-guarded, so a report failure at exactly the one moment Run() called it before the first sync left priorUsageFromDisk permanently empty -- suspectBrownfield could then never fire again for the rest of the process's life, with no metric or retry to recover. Reproduced by calling the prime once with a failing report runner, then again with a succeeding one under the unmodified sync.Once: the second call was a no-op and the guard stayed unprimed forever

Added status.GetDirUsagesStrict (report error returned instead of swallowed; an unreported path falls back to GetDirAllocatedSize from e3 rather than GetDirSize's apparent size). Replaced the primeOnce sync.Once field with a plain `primed bool` guarded by a.mu; primeAppliedQuotasFromDiskOnce now checks it first (a single mutex check once primed, no subprocess) and flips it true only after a nil-error GetDirUsagesStrict read has filled both snapshot maps. syncAllQuotas calls it at the top of every cycle -- a real retry, not a second one-shot attempt -- so a startup failure self-heals the next cycle the report is readable; Run()'s call site is unchanged. Unprimed stays fail-open by design (fail-closed would turn a transient report fault into a first-touch enforcement outage on a healthy node); the window is now observable via two new metrics, nfs_quota_agent_shrink_guard_primed (gauge) and nfs_quota_agent_shrink_guard_prime_failures_total (a never-reset counter), plus ShrinkGuardPrimed()/ShrinkGuardPrimeFailures() accessors on the widened metrics.AgentInfo interface

Two deliberate breakages verified and reverted: (1) routing the prime through status.GetDirUsages instead of GetDirUsagesStrict made TestPrime_ReportErrorDoesNotMarkPrimed fail (the error vanishes into an empty map and primed becomes true off a false negative); (2) restoring the sync.Once guard made TestPrime_RetriesAfterStartupReportFailure fail with 'expected ShrinkGuardPrimed() == true after syncAllQuotas retried the prime', since a sync.Once-guarded attempt never retries after its first (failing) call. Existing TestWatchPVsEventStormAtScale and TestEnsureQuota_EmptyBrownfieldDirectoryAppliesWithoutExtraUsageRead were confirmed to still pass unmodified -- neither drives syncAllQuotas, so the new per-cycle retry call never reaches them
events.scope: internal/agent prime lifecycle (primeAppliedQuotasFromDiskOnce, syncAllQuotas' retry call, ShrinkGuardPrimed/ShrinkGuardPrimeFailures) and internal/metrics' widened AgentInfo surface, exercised through the stubbed CommandRunner seam only

events.summary: #92: currentUsageBytes fetches the whole filesystem-wide usage report to answer one path's usage, with no per-cycle memoization, and a brownfield claim's rejection is permanent until an operator intervenes -- so N such claims cost N identical report subprocess calls, serialized under a.mu, every 30s sync cycle for as long as they remain unresolved. Reproduced by counting report-type runner calls across a syncAllQuotas pass over three brownfield PVs before the fix: three separate calls for the same, already-known-absent answer

Added passUsageSnapshot, declared once per syncAllQuotas pass beside the existing driftReport variables, memoizing only which localPaths the usage report contains -- never a usage value. ensureQuotaMutated is now a wrapper around the new ensureQuotaMutatedWith(ctx, pv, effectiveBytes, snap); the guard consults the snapshot via the new usageForGuard ahead of currentUsageBytes. A path absent from the report answers (0,false) immediately with no further I/O (safe to reuse, since absence already means 'reject' regardless of freshness); a path present always still pays for its own live currentUsageBytes read, so no approving decision's freshness changes. Every caller other than syncAllQuotas' PV loop -- ensureQuota/ensureQuotaMutated, and therefore reconcile_queue.go's watch path -- passes nil, meaning 'always consult a live report,' identical to pre-#92 behavior. Also rate-limited the per-PV rejection slog.Warn to once per path per state transition via a new shrinkGuardRejectWarned set, pruned alongside appliedQuotas and cleared on a later successful apply

Deliberate breakage: made a PRESENT path answer straight from the memo's first-fetch snapshot instead of paying for its own live currentUsageBytes call. TestSyncAllQuotas_PresentPathStillGetsLiveUsageRead failed with 'report calls for the pass = 1, want exactly 2', confirming the present-path live-read guarantee is actually exercised by that assertion; reverted and re-confirmed green
events.scope: internal/agent's syncAllQuotas PV loop, ensureQuotaMutatedWith's guard, and reconcile_queue.go's watch path, exercised through the stubbed CommandRunner seam only

events.summary: #94's allocated-size walk, #93's retrying/observable prime, and #92's per-pass usage-report memoization are implemented, wired into the brownfield guard exactly as scoped in e1, and verified at the level stated in e11

Complete at the unit and static-analysis level against the stubbed CommandRunner seam. A real prjquota-mounted host still needs to confirm, independently of anything provable here: how far st.Blocks*512 actually sits from what each backend charges (XFS assigns by inode-to-project, not by path walk; btrfs qgroups charge shared CoW/reflink extents a per-file walk can't see at all -- the allocated-size walk is a suspicion trigger, not a claim of matching real enforcement); real sparse/preallocated (fallocate, not just truncate) behavior on XFS and ext4 rather than APFS/tmpfs; that an absent path in a real report genuinely always means 'no project ID' on all three backends, the entire premise #92's negative memo rests on; real report-subprocess latency at N PVs, the actual motivation for #92; and whether a late prime reads the same numbers an early one would on a server with active concurrent writers
